title: AuthZ ledger for automated config migrations and forensic rollback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: The Auto-Apply feature for batching/caching recommendations currently performs configuration migrations with minimal attestation and limited forensic traceability. For teams on Dedicated and Private deployments we need a compliance-grade record of who authorized changes, a tamper-evident changelog, and safe rollback primitives that satisfy SOC-type audits and customer security reviews.

Goal: Implement an immutable authorization ledger and change pipeline that ties RBAC approvals to cryptographically-signed config bundles, integrates with KMS/HSM for signatures, enforces policy gates before apply, and produces structured audit events and exportable forensic artifacts. The ledger must support: (1) attested canary applies, (2) time-bound rollback tokens, (3) per-tenant keying for Private deployments, and (4) export hooks to SIEM and long-term WORM storage.

Scope:
- Design an "AuthZ Ledger" service (append-only store) that records change digests, signer identity, approval artifacts (user, approver, policy hash), and pre/post metrics snapshots.
- Extend the Auto-Apply controller to emit signed change bundles and to require a ledger entry before any cross-customer config mutation.
- Add RBAC bindings and an approval workflow: escalation paths, required approvers for high-impact changes, and transient "apply tokens" minted only after approval and ledger entry.
- Integrate with KMS (cloud KMS + HSM option) for signing bundles and for per-customer key isolation in Private deployments.
- Build rollback primitives that accept a signed rollback request; rollback execution must be recorded with a new ledger entry and must support safe canary-and-verify.
- Surface ledger entries and approval state in Console (read-only views) and expose structured audit exports (JSONL) for compliance teams.
- Retention and export: provide WORM export to S3-compatible storage and a SIEM connector for live streaming of audit events.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of Policy Engine; this ticket adds hooks and parity checks only. Deep UX redesign of Console will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger API exists and stores append-only entries with change_digest, signer_id, approver_ids, timestamp, and policy_hash.
Auto-Apply refuses to apply a config migration without a valid signed ledger entry and a matching apply token.
Signatures use KMS-based keys; Private deployments can opt for per-tenant keys via HSM/KMS integration.
Rollback action produces a new ledger entry and supports canary rollback followed by automated verification of traffic/latency metrics.
Console exposes a read-only timeline for each change with links to PR, design doc, and metric snapshots; audit exports are JSONL with schema v1.
Security review completed and documented; export pipeline to SIEM validated in staging with sample customer tenancy.
SRE runbook added with steps for forensic export and manual rollback (including required approvers).
tasks: Design API contract and data model for AuthZ Ledger (sequence numbers, digests, signature fields)
Implement append-only store (Cockroach write-ahead + signed blob store) and HTTP gRPC front-end
Add KMS signing integration and HSM option for Private installs
Modify Auto-Apply controller: require ledger entry and validate signatures before applying
Create apply-token service that mints short-lived tokens post-approval
Add rollback flow with canary and metric validation hooks
Console: read-only timeline UI and export button (JSONL); backend export job to S3
End-to-end tests: staging apply/rollback + ledger tamper tests
Documentation: runbook, compliance playbook, and Confluence design doc
